name: Joe Biden
role: 46th U.S. president (2021-2025); vice president (2009-2017); U.S. senator from Delaware (1973-2009)
summary: Biden is a Democratic centre-left liberal whose record favours unions, a higher minimum wage, higher taxes on the wealthy and corporations, expanded health coverage, climate investment and civil and LGBTQ+ rights, within a capitalist, bipartisan-minded framework. He supports abortion rights, gun limits short of a ban on guns, NATO and allied military strength, Israel with a two-state goal, and a tougher but legal-pathway immigration policy. He frames politics as defending democracy and institutions, and warned in 2025 of oligarchy and a 'tech-industrial complex'.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Called health care 'a right and not a privilege' and expanded ACA subsidies and Medicare drug-price power, but campaigned for a public option rather than a single government payer, and dropped that in 2021.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Urged Congress to raise the federal minimum wage to $15 an hour (from $7.25), defending it against small-business objections in a 2021 town hall and repeating the call in 2024.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Calls himself a capitalist, but his signed record (CHIPS Act, IRA tax credits, antitrust orders) has government steering investment and correcting markets instead of trusting prices alone.

central-planning.rationale: States 'I'm a capitalist' in several speeches and frames his policy as a fairer capitalism with competition rules, not a planned economy.

tax-inheritance.rationale: As a senator he voted Nay on permanently repealing the death tax in 2002 (H.R. 8) and Nay on the 2007 budget-resolution amendments to repeal it (44-55) or raise the exemption to $5 million, voting to keep the estate tax.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Kept Trump-era China tariffs and raised them in May 2024 on EVs, solar cells, steel and critical minerals, and applies Buy American rules to federal projects.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Signed the CHIPS Act ($52 billion for semiconductor production) and IRA clean-energy credits, and said the supply chain should begin in America; the tools are subsidies and tax credits rather than direct state control.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Nominated sitting and new members of the Federal Reserve Board, including Jerome Powell as chair, and speaks of the Fed's inflation role without questioning its existence.

one-party-rule.rationale: Frames the contest as democracy against autocracy and calls free elections and dissent essential; calls autocrats the adversaries of America.

democracy-best.rationale: Told Congress 'with democracy, everything is possible; without it, nothing is' and facilitated a peaceful transfer of power to the candidate he opposed.

natural-rulers.rationale: Roots his politics in 'all of us are created equal' and the Declaration's claim of equal standing, leaving no room for innate rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Said political violence has 'absolutely no place' in America, 'zero place', after January 6 and the attack on Paul Pelosi.

military-superiority.rationale: Signed a record $886 billion defense bill and pledged to modernize the military to 'deter aggression' and stay in the strongest position against competitors.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Said that other nations are defined by geography or ethnicity, but the United States is founded on an idea and is a nation of immigrants.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Said everyone is entitled to a fair shot, 'not a guarantee, but just a fair shot, an even playing field', which stresses opportunity.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Celebrates manufacturing, infrastructure and technology as engines of a better future, including 800,000 new factory jobs.

restore-past-order.rationale: Frames politics as a contest between those who would 'pull America back to the past' and those moving forward, and says 'America cannot go back'.

hereditarian-race.rationale: His racial equity order attributes group disparities to entrenched laws, policies and institutions rather than innate differences.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Condemned Russia's invasion as aggression that threatens the free world and led sanctions to make Putin pay.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Called himself a lifelong supporter of Israel (and has said 'I am a Zionist'), condemned Hamas's aim of destroying the State of Israel and pledged support.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Signed the $1.9 trillion American Rescue Plan and argued stimulus would create millions of jobs, while also stressing deficit reduction later and paying for new plans with taxes on the wealthy.

national-self-determination.rationale: Reaffirmed the Palestinian people's right to self-determination and defended Ukraine's right to live free and choose its own course.

force-without-un.rationale: Ordered strikes on Houthi targets and sent forces for the Gaza pier without a UN Security Council mandate.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Praised Brown v. Board of Education and the fight against segregated schools on its 70th anniversary.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Says the country still needs oil and gas for a decade or more and criticized oil firms for investing too little in production, yet paused federal leasing in 2021 and backs steep emission cuts; the signals point both ways.

elite-replacement.rationale: Condemned the claim that immigrants are 'poison in the blood of our country' and said he would not demonize immigrants.

national-mission.rationale: Said the Afghanistan withdrawal ends 'an era of major military operations to remake other countries' and speaks of leading by the power of America's example.

night-watchman-state.rationale: His record is of expanding the federal role in health, climate, infrastructure and consumer protection well beyond defense, justice and property.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Signed the Respect for Marriage Act protecting interracial marriage as well as same-sex marriage.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Calls 'all of us are created equal' the core idea of America and 'North Star', and insists on equal treatment of all in each address.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Describes Israel as a democracy with a legitimate security claim and a lifelong ally, rejecting Hamas's call for its destruction.

separated-powers.rationale: Praised 'separation of powers, checks and balances' as what has maintained American democracy for nearly 250 years.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: His racial equity order says 'our diversity is one of our country's greatest strengths'.

party-controls-media.rationale: Names a free and independent press among the institutions a free society depends on and warns that the free press is 'crumbling'.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Welcomed Finland and Sweden into NATO, called it the strongest military alliance in history and signed AUKUS.

death-penalty.rationale: On 23 December 2024 he commuted 37 of the 40 federal death sentences to life without parole, 'consistent with the moratorium my administration has imposed', leaving terrorism and hate-motivated mass-murder cases; he wrote that he was 'more convinced than ever' that the federal death penalty should stop.

collective-defense.rationale: Signed the instruments of ratification for Finland and Sweden to join NATO and says America stands with NATO allies, whose alliance exists to secure peace through common defense.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Condemned Russia's 'illegal annexation' of Ukrainian territory and said Ukrainian forces were reclaiming their land.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Proposed a higher top bracket for incomes over $400,000, a billionaire minimum tax and no new taxes below $400,000, a progressive structure the opposite of a flat rate.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Called for a constitutional amendment so that no president is immune from crimes committed in office.

ban-cartels.rationale: Executive Order 14036 says market concentration threatens economic liberty and orders competition enforcement; in his farewell he praised busting the trusts a century ago.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Urges passage of the Equality Act and signed orders extending civil rights protections against discrimination in housing, employment, health care and education.

elective-rulers.rationale: Presents free and fair elections and the will of the people as the basis of rule and condemned efforts to overturn them.

paid-care-work.rationale: Proposed paid family leave and wages for home-care workers, and said family caregivers should 'finally get the pay they deserve'.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Promised to protect and strengthen state Social Security and to veto any cut or higher retirement age; says working people earned those benefits.

corporate-influence.rationale: Called for removing dark money from politics and warned that concentrated wealth threatens democracy; his 2024 address condemned 'unlimited dark money'.

non-intervention.rationale: Backs sanctions and weapons for Ukraine and pressure on the Burmese junta, arguing nations have sovereignty but aggressors must pay a price.

religious-nation.rationale: Defines America by the idea of equality, and said he would 'not ban people because of their faith'.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Called October 7 the deadliest day for the Jewish people since the Holocaust, treating it as an established atrocity.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Signed orders protecting LGBTQ+ people and removed Uganda from the AGOA trade preference over its anti-LGBT law that carries the death penalty for homosexuality.

future-generations.rationale: Said America has 'an obligation not to ourselves, but to our children and our grandchildren' to confront climate change.

arms-reduction.rationale: Extended New START and proposed new arms control and transparency measures to Russia in 2022.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Backs the PRO Act and workers' right to organize, citing unions as the route to higher wages and benefits, including the UAW and building trades.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Expanded the child tax credit during the pandemic, sought to restore it, and backs tax credits and credits for working families as the way to lift incomes.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Announced forgiveness of $10,000 of federal student loans ($20,000 for Pell recipients) and later fixed repayment programs to relieve nearly 4 million borrowers.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: His administration extended the New START Treaty for five years in February 2021, keeping verifiable limits on both arsenals rather than disarming unilaterally, and pledged to pursue further arms control.

reviewHistory.rationale: Extended the New START treaty with Russia rather than disarming unilaterally, keeping the arsenal within mutual limits.

women-suffrage.rationale: Celebrates serving with the first woman vice president and says everyone's right to vote must be protected.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Proposed ending special tax breaks for Big Pharma, Big Oil, private jets and executive pay deductions.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Names 'systemic racism' as one of the gravest challenges in his inaugural and calls to root it out of criminal justice.

(Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

torture-always-illegal.rationale: In July 2007 he introduced a rendition bill that 'prohibits rendering individuals to countries that will torture or mistreat them or to secret, extraterritorial prisons', saying commitment to the rule of law is among the most formidable counterterrorism weapons.

shut-down-tax-havens.rationale: In his April 2021 address to Congress he said companies 'evade taxes through tax havens in Switzerland and Bermuda and the Cayman Islands... It's not right' and promised to reform corporate taxes.

human-caused-global-warming.rationale: His Executive Order 14008 of January 2021, 'Tackling the Climate Crisis at Home and Abroad', puts the climate crisis at the centre of foreign and domestic policy and orders federal action to cut emissions.

prohibit-child-medical-transition.rationale: His Executive Order 14075 (June 2022, 'Advancing Equality for LGBTQI+ Individuals') directs federal action to protect transgender people, including against attempts to restrict their access to care.

notes: Answers rest on his own speeches, orders and signed laws from 2021 to January 2025, plus two Wikipedia articles for record items. His 50-year record changed on several issues (crime and the 1994 bill, the Defense of Marriage Act, the Hyde Amendment, same-sex marriage, the death penalty); the recent clear position is recorded, so same-sex marriage reads +2 on his 2012 and 2022 acts. Statements with no recorded position of his own are null; nothing was filled from party or label. A prior pilot audit was discarded and none of its answers were carried over. Judgment calls: the death penalty (-1: he commuted 37 of 40 federal death sentences but left terrorism and hate-crime cases), empower-police-military (0: more funding but restricted authority), expand-fossil-fuels (0, low: both directions), legalize-drugs (-1: pardons and decriminalization talk, not endorsement of legal recreational drugs). He did not commit publicly to nuclear power, tax on inheritances or the Supreme Court beyond term limits in the sources opened, so those are null. Cited sources were opened in this session as full texts (American Presidency Project) or Wikipedia. Later pass 2026-11-13 (rules 7): sources tagged by kind (executive orders, proclamations and administration policy statements are actions); sixteen answers that cited both an action and words were reduced to the action sources with history, per record over words; death-penalty and keep-nuclear-weapons, which rested only on Wikipedia, now cite his 23 December 2024 commutation statement and the State Department's New START extension statement. New from his 36 Senate years (Voteview, ICPSR 14101, and Stanford Congressional Record speeches): defensive-wars-only, humanitarian-intervention, tax-inheritance (action), surveillance-ok, torture-always-illegal (words); also shut-down-tax-havens, human-caused-global-warming and prohibit-child-medical-transition from existing presidential sources. His Senate votes on the 1996 Defense of Marriage Act (Yea), the 1994 crime bill and Iraq are recorded in Voteview but the same-sex-marriage and crime answers stay with his later acts. The Miller Center copies of his speeches are declined (duplicates of cited American Presidency Project texts or searched without usable hits). Voteview and the Congressional Record hold far more of his Senate record than is mapped here; positions not settled by those votes and speeches stay null.

booksNotUsed.reason: Miller Center copies of presidential speeches; the major ones (inaugural, joint-session address, State of the Union addresses, farewell, Afghanistan, Ukraine, Hamas) are already cited from the American Presidency Project copies, and the rest were searched by keyword (torture, hate, church and state, nuclear power, transgender, voter ID, conscription, work requirements, tax havens, International Criminal Court, climate, nuclear) with usable hits only on the passages cited.
